ladder.title: Bertrand's postulate
ladder.q: Prove that for every integer $n\ge 1$ there is a prime $p$ with $n<p\le 2n$. Deduce that $p_{n+1}<2p_n$ for every $n\ge 1$, where $p_n$ denotes the $n$th prime.
ladder.source: Aigner & Ziegler, Proofs from THE BOOK, Chapter 2 (Bertrand's postulate)
ladder.note: The first unconditional upper bound for prime gaps, proved by elementary estimates on the central binomial coefficient.

ladder.title: Average size and second moment of prime gaps
ladder.source: Folklore consequences of the prime number theorem; the lower bound in (b) is recorded at erdosproblems.com/233 (Erdős Problem #233)
ladder.note: Fixes the natural scale $\log p_n$ for gaps; (b) is the trivial lower bound matching Heath-Brown's conjectured upper bound $N(\log N)^2$.

ladder.title: Westzynthius: gaps are unboundedly larger than average
ladder.q:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$th prime. Prove that
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{\log p_n}=\infty.$$
ladder.source: E. Westzynthius, Über die Verteilung der Zahlen, die zu den n ersten Primzahlen teilerfremd sind, Societas Scientiarum Fennica, Commentationes Physico-Mathematicae 5 (1931), no. 25
ladder.note: Shows that $\infty$ is a limit point of the normalized gaps, via long runs of integers each sharing a factor with the primorial.

ladder.title: Rankin's lower bound for large gaps
ladder.q:
Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that
$$p_{n+1}-p_n>c\,\frac{\log p_n\,\log\log p_n\,\log\log\log\log p_n}{(\log\log\log p_n)^2}$$
for infinitely many $n$.
ladder.source: R. A. Rankin, The difference between consecutive prime numbers, J. London Math. Soc. 13 (1938)
ladder.note: The Erdős–Rankin method: cover an interval by one residue class per small prime, using smooth numbers to handle the hardest part; Erdős Problem 4 asks to make $c$ arbitrarily large.

ladder.title: Long gaps between primes (Ford–Green–Konyagin–Maynard–Tao)
ladder.q:
Prove that for all sufficiently large $X$,
$$\max_{p_n\le X}(p_{n+1}-p_n)\gg\frac{\log X\,\log\log X\,\log\log\log\log X}{\log\log\log X}.$$
ladder.source: K. Ford, B. Green, S. Konyagin, J. Maynard, T. Tao, Long gaps between primes, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 31 (2018), 65–105
ladder.note: Gains a factor $\log\log\log X$ over Rankin (settling Erdős Problem 4 in a strong form) by combining the covering argument with Maynard's sieve weights; improving it further is the residue-class covering question of Green's Problem 46.

ladder.title: Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım: small normalized gaps
ladder.q:
Prove that
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{p_{n+1}-p_n}{\log p_n}=0.$$
ladder.source: D. A. Goldston, J. Pintz, C. Y. Yıldırım, Primes in tuples I, Ann. of Math. (2) 170 (2009), 819–862
ladder.note: Shows that $0$ is a limit point of the normalized gaps, the case $C=0$ of Erdős Problem 5 (normalizing by $\log n$ or $\log p_n$ is equivalent).

ladder.title: Bounded gaps between primes (Maynard)
ladder.q: Prove that for every integer $m\ge 1$ there is a constant $C_m$ such that $p_{n+m}-p_n\le C_m$ for infinitely many $n$. In particular show that $p_{n+1}-p_n\le 600$ for infinitely many $n$.
ladder.source: J. Maynard, Small gaps between primes, Ann. of Math. (2) 181 (2015), 383–413
ladder.note: Multidimensional sieve weights give many primes in a single admissible tuple, which is the engine behind the solution of Erdős Problem 6 and the later rungs.

ladder.title: Monotone runs of prime gaps
ladder.q: Let $d_n=p_{n+1}-p_n$. Prove that for every $m\ge 1$ there are infinitely many $n$ with $d_n<d_{n+1}<\cdots<d_{n+m}$, and infinitely many $n$ with $d_n>d_{n+1}>\cdots>d_{n+m}$.
ladder.source: W. D. Banks, T. Freiberg, C. L. Turnage-Butterbaugh, Consecutive primes in tuples, Acta Arith. 167 (2015), no. 3
ladder.note: Upgrades Maynard's theorem to control which members of a tuple are consecutive primes, settling the Erdős–Turán question (Erdős Problem 6); the same control over consecutive gaps is what Problems 852–853 ask about.

ladder.title: A positive proportion of limit points of normalized gaps
ladder.q: Let $L$ be the set of limit points in $[0,\infty)$ of the sequence $(p_{n+1}-p_n)/\log p_n$. Prove that for any nine real numbers $0\le\beta_1\le\beta_2\le\cdots\le\beta_9$, at least one difference $\beta_j-\beta_i$ with $1\le i<j\le 9$ lies in $L$. Deduce that the Lebesgue measure of $L\cap[0,T]$ is at least $T/8$ for every $T>0$.
ladder.source: W. D. Banks, T. Freiberg, J. Maynard, On limit points of the sequence of normalized prime gaps, Proc. London Math. Soc. (2016), arXiv:1404.5094
ladder.note: The strongest type of result towards Erdős Problem 5 (whether every $C\ge0$ is a limit point); Merikoski (arXiv:1811.03008) later improved the proportion to $1/3$ and showed $L$ has bounded gaps.

ladder.title: Strings of consecutive primes in one residue class (Shiu)
ladder.q: Let $q\ge 1$ and $a$ be integers with $\gcd(a,q)=1$, and let $k\ge 1$. Prove that there are infinitely many $r$ such that the $k$ consecutive primes $p_{r+1},p_{r+2},\ldots,p_{r+k}$ are all congruent to $a$ modulo $q$.
ladder.source: D. K. L. Shiu, Strings of congruent primes, J. London Math. Soc. (2) 61 (2000)
ladder.note: Directly answers Erdős Problem 427 (choose a string of $d$ consecutive primes $\equiv1\bmod d$); it is the nearest proven statement to finding consecutive primes in arithmetic progression (Problem 141), where the differences, not just the residues, must be fixed.

ladder.title: Counting squarefree numbers
ladder.q:
Let $Q(x)$ be the number of squarefree positive integers $n\le x$. Prove that
$$Q(x)=\frac{6}{\pi^2}x+O(\sqrt{x}).$$
ladder.source: Hardy & Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers, Ch. XVIII
ladder.note: The model computation: write the indicator of squarefree numbers as $\sum_{d^2\mid n}\mu(d)$ and sum.

ladder.title: No two elements with square product
ladder.q: For $N\ge1$ let $F_2(N)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that $ab$ is not a perfect square for any two distinct $a,b\in A$. Prove that $F_2(N)$ equals the number of squarefree integers in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, so that $F_2(N)\sim\frac{6}{\pi^2}N$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, A. Sárközy, V. T. Sós, On product representations of powers, I, European J. Combin. 16 (1995), 567–588
ladder.note: The case $k=2$ of the function $F_k(N)$ in Erdős Problem 121: square classes (squarefree kernels) are the right bookkeeping.

ladder.title: Structure and count of powerful numbers
ladder.q:
Call $n\ge1$ powerful if $p\mid n$ implies $p^2\mid n$ for every prime $p$. Prove that every powerful $n$ can be written uniquely as $n=a^2b^3$ with $a,b$ positive integers and $b$ squarefree. Deduce that the number $P(x)$ of powerful $n\le x$ satisfies
$$P(x)=\frac{\zeta(3/2)}{\zeta(3)}\sqrt{x}+O(x^{1/3}).$$
ladder.source: S. W. Golomb, Powerful numbers, Amer. Math. Monthly 77 (1970), 848–852; the asymptotic goes back to P. Erdős and G. Szekeres, Acta Sci. Math. (Szeged) 7 (1934), 95–102
ladder.note: Gives the density of powerful numbers (about $\sqrt{x}$ of them up to $x$), the heuristic baseline for every question about consecutive or additive patterns of powerful numbers.

ladder.title: Consecutive powerful numbers
ladder.q:
(a) Prove that there are no four consecutive positive integers that are all powerful.

(b) Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $n$ and $n+1$ are both powerful.
ladder.source: S. W. Golomb, Powerful numbers, Amer. Math. Monthly 77 (1970), 848–852
ladder.note: Pairs are plentiful via Pell equations and quadruples are impossible mod 4; triples (Erdős Problem 364) sit exactly between what is easy in both directions.

ladder.title: Smooth numbers with one large prime factor
ladder.q:
Let $\Psi(x,y)$ be the number of $n\le x$ all of whose prime factors are at most $y$. Using Mertens' theorem, prove that for each fixed $u\in[1,2]$,
$$\Psi(x,x^{1/u})=(1-\log u)\,x+O\Big(\frac{x}{\log x}\Big)\quad(x\to\infty).$$
ladder.source: Tenenbaum, Introduction to Analytic and Probabilistic Number Theory, Ch. III.5
ladder.note: Computes Dickman's function on $[1,2]$, where $\rho(u)=1-\log u$, by an inclusion-exclusion that uses only one large prime factor.

ladder.title: Consecutive powerful numbers, neither a square
ladder.q: Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that $n$ and $n+1$ are both powerful and neither $n$ nor $n+1$ is a perfect square.
ladder.source: D. T. Walker, Consecutive integer pairs of powerful numbers and related Diophantine equations, Fibonacci Quart. 14 (1976), 111–116
ladder.note: Gives infinitely many counterexamples to part (a) of Erdős Problem 365 (Golomb had found $23^3$, $23^3+1$); part (b), the $(\log x)^{O(1)}$ count, remains open.

ladder.title: Dickman's theorem
ladder.q:
Let $\rho:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be the continuous function with $\rho(u)=1$ for $0<u\le1$ and $u\rho'(u)=-\rho(u-1)$ for $u>1$. Prove that for each fixed $u\ge1$,
$$\Psi(x,x^{1/u})\sim\rho(u)\,x\quad(x\to\infty).$$
ladder.source: K. Dickman, On the frequency of numbers containing prime factors of a certain relative magnitude, Ark. Mat. Astr. Fys. 22A (1930)
ladder.note: Extends the previous rung to all $u$ by an integral-delay recursion; smooth-number counts like this drive the large-gap constructions in prime-patterns.

ladder.title: Products of consecutive integers are never powers (Erdős–Selfridge)
ladder.q: Prove that for integers $n\ge1$, $k\ge2$ and $\ell\ge2$, the product $n(n+1)\cdots(n+k-1)$ is never an $\ell$th power of an integer.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, J. L. Selfridge, The product of consecutive integers is never a power, Illinois J. Math. 19 (1975), 292–301
ladder.note: Erdős Problem 137 asks for the much weaker conclusion 'never powerful' for $k\ge3$, which is open even though 'never a perfect power' is known.

ladder.title: Coprime arithmetic progressions of powerful numbers
ladder.q: Prove that there are infinitely many pairs of positive integers $(N,d)$ with $\gcd(N,d)=1$ such that $N,N+d,N+2d,N+3d$ are all powerful. Prove also that there are infinitely many such pairs with $\gcd(N,d)=1$ for which $N,N+d,N+2d$ are all $3$-full (every prime factor occurs to at least the third power).
ladder.source: P. Bajpai, M. A. Bennett, T. H. Chan, Arithmetic progressions in squarefull numbers, Int. J. Number Theory (2024), arXiv:2302.03113
ladder.note: Resolves Erdős Problem 937; without coprimality the problem is trivial (scale any progression by a suitable square), and the same paper shows under abc that these lengths are optimal.

ladder.title: Five elements with square product (Tao)
ladder.q: For $N\ge1$ let $F_5(N)$ be the largest size of a set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ such that no product of five distinct elements of $A$ is a perfect square. Prove that there is a constant $c>0$ such that $F_5(N)\le(1-c+o(1))N$ as $N\to\infty$.
ladder.source: T. Tao, On product representations of squares, arXiv:2405.11610 (2024)
ladder.note: Answers Erdős Problem 121 in the negative (the conjecture was $F_5(N)=(1-o(1))N$), contrasting with $F_3(N)=(1-o(1))N$ proved by Erdős–Sárközy–Sós.

ladder.title: Dirichlet's approximation theorem
ladder.q:
Let $\alpha$ be an irrational real number. Prove that there are infinitely many pairs of integers $(p,q)$ with $q\ge1$ such that
$$\Big|\alpha-\frac{p}{q}\Big|<\frac{1}{q^2}.$$
ladder.source: Hardy & Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers, Ch. XI
ladder.note: The baseline exponent $2$ that every later rung either improves on (for special numbers) or shows to be essentially optimal.

ladder.title: Liouville's inequality
ladder.q:
Let $\alpha$ be a real algebraic number of degree $d\ge2$. Prove that there is a constant $c(\alpha)>0$ such that
$$\Big|\alpha-\frac{p}{q}\Big|>\frac{c(\alpha)}{q^d}$$
for all integers $p$ and $q\ge1$. Deduce that $\sum_{n\ge1}10^{-n!}$ is transcendental.
ladder.source: Hardy & Wright, An Introduction to the Theory of Numbers, Ch. XI
ladder.note: The basic mechanism of irrationality and transcendence proofs: a number with too-good rational approximations cannot be rational or algebraic of low degree.

ladder.title: Khintchine's theorem
ladder.q: For real $x$ let $\|x\|$ be the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ be non-increasing. Prove that if $\sum_{q\ge1}\psi(q)<\infty$ then for almost every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ the inequality $\|q\alpha\|<\psi(q)$ has only finitely many solutions $q\in\mathbb{N}$, while if $\sum_{q\ge1}\psi(q)=\infty$ then for almost every $\alpha$ it has infinitely many solutions.
ladder.source: A. Khintchine, Einige Sätze über Kettenbrüche, mit Anwendungen auf die Theorie der Diophantischen Approximationen, Math. Ann. 92 (1924)
ladder.note: The convergence half is Borel–Cantelli; the divergence half needs monotonicity, and removing it (with coprimality) is exactly the Duffin–Schaeffer problem.

ladder.title: Irrationality of the Lambert series at 1/2 (Erdős)
ladder.q:
Prove that
$$\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{2^n-1}=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{\tau(n)}{2^n}$$
is irrational, where $\tau(n)$ is the number of divisors of $n$.
ladder.source: P. Erdős, On arithmetical properties of Lambert series, J. Indian Math. Soc. (N.S.) 12 (1948), 63–66
ladder.note: The case $A=\mathbb{N}$ of Erdős Problem 257 and the case $t=2$ of Problem 1049: the binary expansion of the sum is controlled by the divisor function.

ladder.title: Borwein's irrationality of q-harmonic type series
ladder.q:
Let $q\ge2$ be an integer and $r\ne0$ a rational number with $r\ne-q^n$ for all $n\ge1$. Prove that
$$\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{1}{q^n+r}$$
is irrational.
ladder.source: P. B. Borwein, On the irrationality of Σ 1/(q^n+r), J. Number Theory 37 (1991), 253–259
ladder.note: Settles Erdős Problem 1050 ($q=2$, $r=-3$) and the integer-$t$ case of Problem 1049 via Padé approximation; the rational non-integer $t$ case of 1049 stays open.

ladder.title: Roth's theorem
ladder.q:
Let $\alpha$ be a real algebraic irrational number and $\varepsilon>0$. Prove that there are only finitely many pairs of integers $(p,q)$ with $q\ge1$ such that
$$\Big|\alpha-\frac{p}{q}\Big|<\frac{1}{q^{2+\varepsilon}}.$$
ladder.source: K. F. Roth, Rational approximations to algebraic numbers, Mathematika 2 (1955), 1–20
ladder.note: Shows Dirichlet's exponent $2$ is sharp for every algebraic irrational, improving Liouville's $d$ all the way down.

ladder.title: Littlewood's conjecture for cubic fields (Cassels–Swinnerton-Dyer)
ladder.q:
For real $x$ let $\|x\|$ be the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Let $K$ be a real cubic number field and let $\alpha,\beta\in K$ be such that $1,\alpha,\beta$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Prove that
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\,\|n\alpha\|\,\|n\beta\|=0.$$
ladder.source: J. W. S. Cassels, H. P. F. Swinnerton-Dyer, On the product of three homogeneous linear forms and indefinite ternary quadratic forms, Philos. Trans. Roy. Soc. London Ser. A 248 (1955), 73–96
ladder.note: Littlewood's conjecture is trivial unless both $\alpha,\beta$ are badly approximable; cubic pairs are the most natural such pairs, and this is the case proved.

ladder.title: The Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture (Koukoulopoulos–Maynard)
ladder.q:
Let $\psi:\mathbb{N}\to[0,\infty)$ be any function and let $\varphi$ be Euler's totient function. Prove that for almost every $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ the inequality
$$\Big|\alpha-\frac{a}{q}\Big|<\frac{\psi(q)}{q}$$
has infinitely many solutions in integers $a,q$ with $q\ge1$ and $\gcd(a,q)=1$ if and only if $\sum_{q\ge1}\varphi(q)\psi(q)/q=\infty$.
ladder.source: D. Koukoulopoulos, J. Maynard, On the Duffin–Schaeffer conjecture, Ann. of Math. (2) 192 (2020), 251–307
ladder.note: Removes the monotonicity hypothesis from Khintchine's theorem (with reduced fractions), resolving Erdős Problem 999.

ladder.title: Exceptions to Littlewood have dimension zero (Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss)
ladder.q:
For real $x$ let $\|x\|$ be the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. Prove that the set of pairs $(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb{R}^2$ with
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}n\,\|n\alpha\|\,\|n\beta\|>0$$
has Hausdorff dimension $0$.
ladder.source: M. Einsiedler, A. Katok, E. Lindenstrauss, Invariant measures and the set of exceptions to Littlewood's conjecture, Ann. of Math. (2) 164 (2006), 513–560
ladder.note: The strongest known result toward the Littlewood conjecture (Erdős Problem 495), obtained by measure rigidity for diagonal actions on $\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}_3(\mathbb{Z})$.

ladder.title: Irrationality of the sum over primes (Tao–Teräväinen)
ladder.q:
Let $\omega(n)$ be the number of distinct prime factors of $n$. Prove that
$$\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{\omega(n)}{2^n}=\sum_{p\ \mathrm{prime}}\frac{1}{2^p-1}$$
(verify this identity first) and that this number is irrational.
ladder.source: T. Tao, J. Teräväinen, Quantitative correlations and some problems on prime factors of consecutive integers, arXiv:2512.01739 (2025)
ladder.note: Settles Erdős Problem 69 and the case $A=$ primes of Problem 257, extending Erdős's $A=\mathbb{N}$ rung; it needs correlation estimates for $\omega(n)$ and $\omega(n+h)$ in place of the divisor-function structure.
